CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C lab work found on routine physical screening.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents after hepatitis C antibody test returned positive during routine physical examination. Patient reports feeling fine and was surprised by the positive result. Denies prior diagnosis of hepatitis C. Reports history of intravenous drug use in the past but has been clean for over 15 years. Currently drinks beer occasionally, about one per day, less than in the past. Smokes one to two cigarettes per day and reports difficulty quitting. Denies current medical conditions other than the hepatitis C finding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No other medical conditions reported besides hepatitis C.

MEDICATIONS
Patient reports not taking any medications.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Family history significant for hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
History of intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Current alcohol use: beer occasionally, approximately one per day. Current tobacco use: one to two cigarettes per day. Patient is married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals reviewed and within normal limits. General appearance: no distress, no jaundice. Cardiovascular: regular rate and rhythm with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: bowel sounds present, soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Musculoskeletal: no gait disturbance or edema.

RESULTS
Hepatitis C antibody: positive. Liver panel: AST elevated at 39; ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection. Plan includes confirmation of diagnosis with additional blood work including HCV RNA and HCV genotype testing. Liver ultrasound with elastography ordered to assess for fibrosis and determine severity of liver disease. Family screening recommended with hepatitis C antibody test for wife and children. Follow-up appointment in three weeks. Discussed smoking and alcohol as additional risk factors to address. Patient to receive orders from nurse and assistance scheduling appointments with family doctor.
